assessments.reasoning: Five contiguous parts cover the official 74,234-byte detail with receipt SHA-256 b59dd3a70a92813134fbd536f2e7593aadfcf3abfbdfd88d102360eb66c9cca3. isDeprecatedLicenseId is false. seeAlso and crossRef.url both contain https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/3.0/de/legalcode. crossRef.match is the string “false”.

The official repository API identifies v3.29.0 as an unsigned annotated tag and gives its target type as commit and target SHA as 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. The NC-ND detail was opened at that target.

The cited Creative Commons URL returned the German legal-code page with the full NC-ND title and publisher identifier “CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 DE”. The page separately links deed.de and declares /licenses/by-nc-nd/3.0/de/legalcode.de as its HTML canonical. The /legalcode capture identifies the citation destination.

challenge.method: Checked whether the NC-only detail, an unported edition, the linked deed, or the declared /legalcode.de canonical could satisfy both the identifier and URL fields. Compared the opening and §3(a) wording.
challenge.results: The pinned ID carries NC, ND, 3.0 and DE, and both citation fields retain /by-nc-nd/3.0/de/legalcode. The SPDX heading adds “Creative Commons” and §3(a) begins “den” where the publisher has “Den”. These differences are consistent with the limited citation claim.

limitations: The finding covers one generated detail at one commit and one measured publisher representation. SPDX’s deprecation field describes the identifier in that release. Byte or legal equivalence, publisher currency, translation, project-wide licensing, downstream grants and redistribution rights remain outside the finding.
